method: Use 396 mapped-prompt texts and exactly five human readers per text (1,980 reader rows). Standardize items and indices within prompt, average reader indices, then standardize the text predictor. Regress the writer’s own standardized intensity on mean reader fit, with prompt intercepts and reader-mean unpleasantness. Refit using 2,000 whole-original-writer resamples; all 396 writer clusters, paired profile substitutions and intensity secondary are retained.
next: File the complete magnitude and secondary-route evidence in the final packet; keep software-engine calibration and causal or biological interpretations separate.
public_wording: The reader-derived trigger-fit slope is inconclusive with limited sensitivity; direct reader-attributed intensity has a supported secondary association with writer intensity, while the same-rater comparison is scale only.

scope: The primary does not establish a useful trigger-to-intensity route at the declared minimum slope. The direct-intensity secondary measures a distinct route and cannot rescue that primary. Each reader’s fit versus her own intensity uses overlapping same-rater judgments, so its association is by construction and cannot count as independent backward inference. These are human panels, not measured performance of the proposed software engine. This analyst-added question has no H12 theory tag.
